blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: A fixed group $G$ will admit many different cobounded actions on different hyperbolic metric spaces. Abbott, Balasubramanya, and Osin in [@ABO19] show that the set of equivalence classes of cobounded hyperbolic actions of a group $G$ carries a natural partial order; see Section [\[sec:prelim\]](#sec:prelim){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:prelim"}. The resulting poset is called the *poset of hyperbolic structures* on $G$, denoted $\mathcal{H}(G)$. Roughly speaking, one action is larger than another if the smaller space can be formed by equivariantly collapsing some subspaces of the larger.

In this section, we review the partial order on cobounded group actions introduced in [@ABO19]. Fix a group $G$. If $G$ acts coboundedly on two metric spaces $X$ and $Y$, we say $G\curvearrowright X$ *is dominated by* $G\curvearrowright Y$, written $G\curvearrowright X \preceq G\curvearrowright Y$, if there exists a coarsely $G$--equivariant coarsely Lipschitz map $Y\to X$. In this section, we review Croke-Kleiner admissible groups [@CK02] and the associated Bass-Serre space, a notion defined in [@HRSS22].

::: defn
A *graph of groups* $\mathcal{G} = (\Gamma, \{G_{\mu}\}, \{G_{\alpha} \}, \{\tau_{\alpha} \})$ is a connected graph $\Gamma$ together with a group ${G}_{\sigma}$ for each $\sigma \in  V(\Gamma) \cup E(\Gamma)$ (here $V(\Gamma)$ and $E(\Gamma)$ denote vertices and edges), and an injective homomorphism $\tau_{\alpha} \colon {G}_{\alpha} \to {G}_{\mu}$ for each oriented edge $\alpha$, where $\mu$ denotes the terminal vertex of $\alpha$.

blocks.title: Theorem 1.1
blocks.content:
whose statement we recall for the convenience of the reader.
Theorem 1.1. Let M be a non-geometric 3-manifold with empty or toroidal boundary. If the
torus decomposition of M contains any of the following, then π1(M) is H–inaccessible:
(1) a hyperbolic piece which contains a boundary torus of M;
(2) two hyperbolic pieces glued along a torus;
(3) an isolated non-elementary Seifert ﬁbered piece; or
(4) a non-elementary maximal graph manifold component.

blocks.title: H–accessibility of finitely generated 3-manifold groups
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:Boundary label="sec:Boundary"} In this section, we explain how one might reduce the study of $\mathcal{H}$--accessibility of all finitely generated 3--manifold groups to the case of compact, orientable, irreducible, $\partial$--irreducible 3--manifold groups. In particular, we show that for any hyperbolic 3-manifold $M$ without rank-1 cusps, if $\pi_1(M)$ is finitely generated then it is $\mathcal H$-accessible.
